One request per second is the *reservoir*

evidence.quote: By default, the SDK records the first request each second, and five percent of any additional requests. One request per second is the *reservoir*. claim: If the X-Ray SDK reads sampling rules from a local JSON document, each instance performs sampling independently, which increases the overall percentage of requests sampled, and you must redeploy your code to update the rules; rules configured in the X-Ray service can be managed without additional deployments.
question: Why define X-Ray sampling rules in the console instead of in a local file?

values.display: manage rules without making additional deployments

evidence.quote: You can configure the X-Ray SDK to read sampling rules from a JSON document that you include with your code. However, when you run multiple instances of your service, each instance performs sampling independently. This causes the overall percentage of requests sampled to increase because the reservoirs of all of the instances are effectively added together. Additionally, to update local sampling rules, you must redeploy your code.
evidence.title: Configuring sampling rules

evidence.quote: Because the rules are configured in the service, you can manage rules without making additional deployments.
